findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the prep table fail to hold proper cold holding temperatures during today’s visit. A part has been ordered for the cooler which should deliver either today or tomorrow. Time as a control is in use for items in the prep cooler until the repairs are complete. Inspector observed a dry erase board for time monitoring, but a loading time was not listed. An employee was able to tell the inspector what time the cooler was loaded, and the cooler was within the 4-hour window. Ensure time records are kept at ALL TIMES. Inspector will follow-up on July 24, 2026 to ensure the prep table is repaired. 

The prep table was also not functioning during today’s visit. The PIC was aware of the issue and is using ice baths in the cooler. However, the ice baths are inadequate for cold holding. A tray of sliced tomatoes in the prep cooler measured 53.3F with a probe thermometer. The PIC stated that the prep table was loaded at 11am. All time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods in the prep cooler (sliced tomatoes, diced tomatoes, sliced cheese, cut lettuce, dairy based sauces, deli ham) were discarded at 3pm. The service technician claims that the coils of the prep cooler are clogged with grease. The technician is currently working to clean the coils and repair the equipment. Until the repair is complete, staff must use time as a control for items in the prep table. Ice baths are not required in addition to time as a control, but are useful for quality. 
A follow-up will be conducted on July 13, 2026 to ensure proper cold holding is restored in the walk-ins and prep table.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no quaternary ammonia sanitizer available in the kitchen. The PIC was informed and a sanitizer bucket was prepared. Ensure there is sanitizer available in the kitchen at all times to promote proper sanitization.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the walk-in cooler, walk-in freezer, and prep table fail to hold proper cold holding temperatures during today’s visit. A baked potato in the walk-in measured 52.5F with a probe thermometer. The PIC stated that the cooler only started warming this early afternoon. All time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food were moved to the beer cooler until repairs can be completed. 
The prep table was also not functioning during today’s visit. The PIC was aware of the issue and is using ice baths in the cooler. However, the ice baths are inadequate for cold holding. A tray of sliced tomatoes in the prep cooler measured 53.3F with a probe thermometer. The PIC stated that the prep table was loaded at 11am. All time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods in the prep cooler (sliced tomatoes, diced tomatoes, sliced cheese, cut lettuce, dairy based sauces, deli ham, and shell egg) were discarded at 3pm. Until the repair is complete, staff must use time as a control for items in the prep table. Ice baths are not required in addition to time as a control, but are useful for quality. Staff plan to use dry erase marker on the glass lid of the table to indicate discard time for each item.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed flies present in the dish area of the facility. Old frying equipment is being stored on the ground next to the triple sink. The PIC also stated that the lid to the grease trap is damaged. This, along with the moisture from the triple sink, is contributing to fly harborage. Ensure the old equipment is removed and the grease trap lid is repaired. Inspector will follow up on August 4, 2026 to ensure there are no pests present in the facility.

The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a pork loin thawing in standing water in the triple sink. The faucet was running over another container of thawing chicken. The PIC was informed that thawing must be conducted under running water or refrigeration at all times. The pork was moved to the walk-in cooler during the inspection. Ensure proper thawing practices are followed to prevent pathogen growth.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no quaternary ammonia test strips available in the facility. Quaternary ammonia tablets are used in sanitizing buckets, and chlorine is used in the dish machine. The facility had only chorine test strips available. The PIC was informed and test strips were acquired. Ensure both types of test strips are available at all times to properly monitor sanitizer concentrations.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Observed the following structures in the building in need of repair:
1. Walk-in cooler-to-freezer door has exposed foam insulation and raw wood to the right of the frame, as well as rags pressed into the holes of the freezer door
2. The walk-in freezer was observed to have heavy ice accumulation as well as food debris on the floor
3. The fan in the dish area was observed soiled with dust and debris

Ensure the floors, ceilings, and walls of the facility are constructed such that they are smooth and easily cleanable. Untreated wood can be painted or stained. Insulation needs to be covered with silicone or another non-porous material. The holes need to be patched and painted. Rags are not an appropriate material for floors, walls, or ceilings in a food preparation/storage space.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Observed CFM on duty to not have additional allergen training certification. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: 2-301.12: (A) Observed employee not use barrier to turn off faucet after washing hands. Use a barrier, such as a paper towel, to turn off faucet after hand washing. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: 2-301.14: Observed employee put on new gloves without washing hands. Wash hand whenever new gloves are used.  FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.
